candidates.name: policy_constraint_enforcement
candidates.description: The agent must recognize when a user request would violate a policy constraint encoded in the environment (e.g., basic-economy is non-modifiable, cancellation only allowed within a window, refund only with insurance for specific reasons, items can only be exchanged within the same product line) and refuse to perform the disallowed action even when the user applies social pressure, emotional appeals, or claims an exception. A failure on this capability typically looks like the agent calling a state-changing tool whose effect contradicts policy, or asserting success when the action should have been refused.

example_trajectories.note: Agent correctly refuses to add insurance to an existing reservation despite persistent user pressure.
Agent updates the reservation to a new origin/destination (LAX/ATL→LAS) despite policy forbidding origin/destination changes.
Agent removes checked bags and refunds them, which is forbidden, while user said to accept refusal.
Agent processes 11 cancellations/returns even though many of those orders were not eligible.

candidates.name: multi_step_transaction_completion
candidates.description: The user request requires two or more sequential, dependent state-changing tool calls (e.g., update flight + update baggage + update passenger; cancel one reservation then book another; modify multiple pending orders; return multiple items in one action). The agent must complete every required step rather than dropping, skipping, or stopping after the first sub-action. A failure looks like only some of the necessary state-changing actions being executed, or the agent declaring success after only partial completion.

example_trajectories.note: Three changes requested (flights, passenger, baggage) — agent did flights & passenger but botched the baggage payment, dropping a step.
User asked to modify two pending t-shirt orders; agent only modified one and stopped.
User asked to update address on user profile and on all orders; agent missed all 7 expected order address updates.
User asked to cancel all upcoming reservations; agent only cancelled some, skipping expected ones.

candidates.name: numerical_and_payment_reasoning
candidates.description: The task requires arithmetic over money: computing totals, fees, refunds, change fees, budget caps, splitting payment across multiple instruments (gift cards, certificates, credit cards), or comparing totals to a user-stated cap. The agent must produce numerically correct values and respect budget constraints; quoting wrong totals, mis-splitting payments, or proceeding when a budget cap is exceeded counts as LACKING. Pure look-ups with no arithmetic do not require this capability (NA).

example_trajectories.note: Required reasoning about payment split across two gift cards, a certificate, and a credit card to minimize CC charge — agent did not produce the correct optimal split.
Agent miscomputed/ignored the change-fee waiver constraint and accepted a change exceeding the user's budget.
User has a credit limit lower than the order total — agent must compute the shortfall and act accordingly.
Required calculating cost of upgrading two passengers; agent skipped the calculate step and committed an upgrade outside the user's $650 cap.

candidates.name: constraint_aware_option_selection
candidates.description: The user specifies multiple constraints on a desired option (cheapest, fastest, departing after 8am, direct preferred, specific cabin, specific color/size/material, must be compatible with X) and the agent must filter the candidate set returned by search/list tools and pick the option that satisfies ALL constraints, not just some. Failure looks like the agent picking an option that violates one of the user's stated constraints, or asking the user to choose when the search results unambiguously identify the right option.

example_trajectories.note: User wanted cheapest economy departing after 11am with two specific certificates for payment; agent booked a flight without verifying all constraints jointly.
Exchanged keyboard with user-specified switch/backlight/size constraints; agent picked a substitute that did not match the requirement set the user explicitly stated.
User wanted nonstop economy arriving before 7am with specific cabin and date — agent picked flights that did not satisfy the time constraint.
Same exchange task as retail:1 but agent correctly matched all keyboard and thermostat attribute constraints.

candidates.name: claim_verification_against_system
candidates.description: The user asserts a fact (membership level, that they have insurance, that a reservation was booked recently, that they were told something by a previous agent, the number of passengers on a reservation) that may be false. The agent must check the authoritative system data (get_user_details, get_reservation_details, get_order_details) before acting on the user's claim, and reject the request if the claim is contradicted by the data. Failure looks like the agent acting on the unverified claim, or claiming the user is correct without checking.

example_trajectories.note: User claims to be Gold; agent verifies via get_user_details, finds Silver, and answers based on real status.
User claims booking was 10 hours ago; agent checks reservation timestamp and refuses to honor the cancellation request.
User lies about having insurance; agent cancels and refunds anyway without verifying insurance status against the reservation record.
User claims wrong passenger count; agent should double-check against reservation but issues a $300 certificate (incorrect amount) without correctly verifying.

candidates.name: conditional_instruction_following
candidates.description: The user gives instructions of the form "If X happens, then do Y; otherwise do Z" or "only do X if cost < $K" or "prefer A but accept B if A is unavailable". The agent must (a) detect the relevant condition during the conversation, (b) take the branch the user actually specified, and (c) NOT volunteer the conditional fallback unprompted. Failure looks like the agent taking a fallback branch when the precondition was never triggered, or ignoring the cap/condition and proceeding.

example_trajectories.note: User said to upgrade only if total < $1000; agent proceeded with the upgrade without confirming the price gate was met.
User said "if removing one item is not possible, then ..." — agent took the fallback branch without first attempting/confirming the primary path.
User wanted to downgrade only if removing a passenger was disallowed; agent applied the fallback even though it was conditional.
User had a $200 budget cap; agent correctly transferred to human rather than violating the cap.

candidates.name: information_gathering_before_action
candidates.description: Before invoking any state-changing tool (book, modify, cancel, exchange, return, update_passengers, send_certificate), the agent must first gather all information needed to make that action correct: get_user_details, the appropriate get_reservation_details / get_order_details, and any get_product_details for items being swapped. Failure looks like a state-changing call made without first reading the relevant records, or with stale/wrong identifiers because the agent skipped the lookup step.

example_trajectories.note: Agent issued a $150 certificate but never read get_reservation_details for the relevant reservation, missing key context.
Agent cancelled one reservation without first getting details on all 7 user reservations to identify which qualified.
Agent attempted return-related actions without doing the full set of order/product lookups expected.
Agent did all required lookups (find_user, get_order, get_product x2) before exchanging items.

candidates.name: aggregation_across_records
candidates.description: The task requires the agent to look up multiple records (reservations, orders, line items, gift cards, certificates) and then aggregate or compare across them: sum balances, find duplicates, find records meeting a duration/price threshold, identify which of N records is the right one, or compute total savings across multiple modifications. The agent must hold the aggregated view in mind and act on it. Failure looks like the agent reasoning over only one record when many are relevant, or producing an aggregate (sum / count / 'which one') that is wrong.

example_trajectories.note: User asked for total savings across downgrading multiple business reservations to economy; agent only processed one reservation.
Agent had to find which of 7 reservations to cancel based on timing/location overlap; agent did not correctly identify the right two.
User wanted all flights longer than 4 hours cancelled; agent did not correctly partition reservations by duration.
Required identifying the gift card with smallest balance among several — agent used the wrong gift card.

candidates.name: handling_concurrent_user_intents
candidates.description: The user introduces multiple distinct intents in a single message, or pivots to a new intent mid-conversation. The agent must track all intents and address each, rather than acting only on the most recently mentioned one or dropping earlier ones. This is distinct from multi-step transaction completion: there, the steps are dependent sub-actions of one intent; here, the intents are independent goals (e.g., 'cancel A, change B, and tell me the cost of C'). Failure looks like the agent answering only one intent and never returning to the others.

example_trajectories.note: User raised a new intent (check cost of other upcoming flights) mid-conversation; agent did not address it.
User combined cancellations + a flight change request; agent never executed the full set of intents.
User asked for passenger change + cabin upgrade + bag addition in one message; agent dropped the multi-intent thread.
User raised several check + change requests across two orders in one conversation; agent did not address all of them.
